zh.question: 同一把尺下天体差多少？同一座星系转个方向又会看到什么？
zh.observe: 先在共同线性标尺上比较天体直径，再沿太阳系、银河系、本星系群、拉尼亚凯亚和可观测范围找结构归属。进入星系结构观察，把同一银河从正面转到侧面，追踪盘内的太阳定位环，分别检查盘、中央核球与棒、稀疏恒星晕；再比较旋涡、椭圆、不规则星系，以及星团与星系群的不同层次。案例切换不是演化进度。最后沿同一物理标尺从地球或太阳连续拉远，区分距离锚点、物理轮廓和示意纹理。

academic.title: 同一长度单位跨越多个量级
academic.body: 模型始终以 km 保存距离，滑杆控制视野宽度的对数而不是把每个天体的半径分别取对数。同一帧内的几何投影保持线性。km、AU 和光年是不同大小的长度单位；超小天体转换为定位符，定位符与真实直径明确分开。大犬座 VY 使用 2012 年约 1420 个太阳半径的光球估计；St2-18 由 2012 年光度与温度推得约 2150 个太阳半径，依赖不确定的距离与星团归属。它们是估计案例，不是最大恒星排行榜。

academic.title: 银河系的空间结构
academic.body: 银河系是棒旋星系，包括扁平恒星盘、中央核球与棒、较稀疏恒星晕和气体等成分。太阳位于盘内，距中心约二万六千光年；本场景取盘半径约五万光年作结构参照。改变视角只改变投影，不重新分布恒星：正面便于找旋臂，侧面便于比较盘与晕的厚度。旋涡、椭圆和不规则是形态案例，不是所有星系必经的演化序列。星团是恒星集合，能作为星系的组成部分；星系群的成员则是多座星系。不能靠亮点数量或圆不圆作统一分类。暗物质晕由引力效应间接推断；本章的可见星点晕只代表恒星晕。中心黑洞主导邻近区域，并不把整个银河变成巨大的太阳系。

academic.title: 地图是有边界的重建
academic.body: 银河系的外观模型根据内部观测重建，而不是从外面拍摄的完整照片。本星系群不仅有银河、仙女座和三角座星系，还包含大、小麦哲伦云等约 50 个矮星系。室女座星系团是另一个邻近结构，不包含本星系群；按拉尼亚凯亚的流向重建，两者都处于这一广大区域，但边界取决于观测和模型，超星系团整体通常不受自身引力束缚。宇宙网是大尺度分布形态，不是容纳拉尼亚凯亚的独立外壳。结构路径图不按比例；可观测范围画面与连续镜头终点共用一套统计示意网，中心定位符并非超星系团直径。远处丝线、结点与小光点不是个别星系的实测位置或大小，不能凭画面测量。最远端的长度表示今天的空间距离量级，不等于光走过的年数；本图不模拟宇宙膨胀或光行回溯时间。

zh.misconception: 光年是距离；太阳系、星团、星系和星系群是不同层次。星系转到侧面不会变成另一种星系；形态类别也不是必然的演化顺序。可观测范围以观察者为参照，不说明地球是宇宙物理中心，视界不是宇宙边墙。
zh.boundary: 地球表面、星点分布与星系外观为结构插画。所有十字和空心小圈都表示位置，不是被放大的真实尺寸。星系方向为示意，银河晕范围非精确边界，本星系群的小星系点只是抽样，不是成员普查。天体对比只比较直径，不表示质量或实际间隔；大角星采用约 25.4 个太阳半径的估计。结构图不按尺寸和距离比例；连续镜头的大尺度丝线和光点也不能用标尺测量。可观测视界不是整个宇宙的物理边缘。 新增星系观察使用稳定的教学点群与三维空间，点数和亮度不是实测恒星数；各案例和星团放大图独立取景，没有共同尺寸标尺。本星系群可旋转图只说明成员归属，位置、尺寸和方向不可量取。正面与侧面使用同一组几何，不计算星系演化或恒星轨道。

narration.label: 把两位放在一起比
narration.text: 先把地球和木星并排放好。木星大得多！请太阳进来，木星又变小了；再看看大角星，太阳也不算大。我们比的是直径，大家用同一把尺，排在一起并不表示它们真的挨得这么近。 再请来名字像编号的巨大恒星。按这里的估计，有的放在太阳的位置，轮廓能伸到土星轨道附近。我们先感受这个“大”，再慢慢了解科学家怎样估计它。
narration.cue: 依次选择三组大小对比，或拖动滑杆，追踪留下来的同一天体。

narration.label: 大球和大家庭不同
narration.text: 太阳和绕着它走的行星组成太阳系。银河里有许多恒星，太阳只是其中一颗；银河与仙女座等大星系以及许多小星系组成了本星系群。本星系群与室女座星系团是不同的邻居，却都出现在拉尼亚凯亚区域的流向重建里。宇宙网说的是这些结构如何分布，并不是下一层壳。
narration.cue: 打开“看看住在哪里”，沿五站结构路径走到可观测范围；另点开室女座星系团对照与宇宙网局部图。

narration.label: 转个方向看银河
narration.text: 先找出银河里的太阳定位环。正面看，星光连成旋臂；转到侧面，同一片星光变成薄盘，中央鼓起，周围还有稀疏的恒星晕。太阳始终留在盘内。再看看平滑的椭圆星系和不对称的不规则星系，这些是不同案例，不是一座星系按顺序变形。星团则是星系里的一群恒星，不能把它当成缩小的星系。
narration.cue: 进入星系结构章，选择正面、侧面并拖动旋转；关闭与重新打开盘、核球和恒星晕，最后比较星团的归属图与独立放大图。

narration.label: 银河之外
narration.text: 带着太阳在银河里的位置，选择从地球或太阳连续拉远。为了容纳遥远轨道，就连太阳的圆盘也会小得看不见；定位符没有把它偷偷放大。银河并不孤单，本星系群还有许多小星系，室女座星系团是另一个邻居。更远处的宇宙网是分布示意，最后的虚线是我们所在位置的观测范围，不是宇宙的一堵墙。今天的距离也不是光旅行的时间。
narration.cue: 进入连续拉远章，从所选天体经过银河、本星系群与拉尼亚凯亚量级，抵达可观测范围；对照画面的线性标尺与位置标签。

en.question: How do bodies compare on one ruler, and what does turning a galaxy reveal?
en.observe: Compare body diameters on one linear ruler, then follow the structural address from the Solar System through the Milky Way, Local Group, Laniakea and observable region. In the galaxy study, turn the same Milky Way from face-on to edge-on, track the Sun locator in the disk, and inspect the disk, central bulge and bar, and sparse stellar halo. Compare spiral, elliptical and irregular forms, then distinguish star clusters from galaxy groups. Changing cases is not an evolutionary clock. Finally zoom continuously from Earth or the Sun, distinguishing distance anchors, physical outlines and illustrative texture.

academic.title: One length system across many orders of magnitude
academic.body: Distances remain in kilometers. The slider changes the logarithm of view width; it does not separately take logarithms of body radii. Geometry within each frame remains a linear projection. Kilometers, AU and light-years are all length units. Subpixel bodies switch to explicit position symbols rather than silently enlarged disks. VY Canis Majoris uses a 2012 photospheric estimate of about 1420 solar radii. St2-18 uses about 2150 solar radii inferred from 2012 luminosity and temperature values, conditional on uncertain distance and cluster membership. These are estimated examples, not a largest-star ranking.

academic.title: The structure of the Milky Way
academic.body: The Milky Way is a barred spiral with a flattened stellar disk, central bulge and bar, sparse stellar halo, gas and other components. The Sun lies in the disk about 26,000 light-years from the centre; a rounded 50,000-light-year disk radius provides a structural reference here. Changing the view changes projection rather than reshuffling stars: face-on reveals arms, while edge-on compares disk and halo depth. Spiral, elliptical and irregular are morphological cases, not a compulsory evolutionary sequence. Star clusters are stellar collections that can belong to a galaxy; galaxy groups contain multiple galaxies. Dot counts and roundness do not define a universal classification. Dark matter is inferred from gravity; the visible halo dots in this chapter represent the stellar halo only. The central black hole governs nearby orbits, not the whole galaxy as a giant Solar System.

academic.title: A reconstruction with defined limits
academic.body: The external Milky Way view is reconstructed from observations made inside it, not photographed from outside. Beyond the Milky Way, the Local Group includes Andromeda, Triangulum and around 50 dwarf galaxies such as the Magellanic Clouds. The Virgo Cluster is a separate nearby structure, not a container for the Local Group. In a Laniakea flow reconstruction both occupy the wider region, but its boundary depends on observations and the model, and the supercluster is generally not bound as a whole. The cosmic web is a pattern of large-scale distribution, not a separate shell around Laniakea. Address diagrams are not to scale; the observable-region view and the continuous camera's endpoint share one statistical illustration, and the central locator is not the supercluster's diameter. Distant filaments, knots and points are not measured positions or sizes of individual galaxies and cannot be measured from the picture. The far-end length is an approximate present-day spatial distance, not light-travel time; expansion and lookback time are not simulated.

en.misconception: A light-year is a distance. Solar systems, star clusters, galaxies and galaxy groups are different levels. An edge-on view does not change a galaxy’s category, and morphology is not a compulsory evolutionary sequence. An observer-centred observable region does not make Earth the physical centre of the universe; its horizon is not a wall.
en.boundary: Earth’s surface, individual point distribution and external galaxy appearance are illustrations. Crosshairs and tiny open circles show locations, not inflated physical sizes. Directions are schematic, halo limits are not precise boundaries, and the small-galaxy marks are a sample, not a Local Group census. Body comparisons show diameters, not masses or separations; Arcturus uses an estimated 25.4 solar radii. Structure diagrams have no size or distance scale, and filaments and points in the continuous long-range camera cannot be measured with its ruler. The observable horizon is not the physical edge of the whole universe. The galaxy study uses stable teaching populations in 3D, not measured star counts or photometry. Cases and cluster close-ups are framed independently, without a common size ruler. The rotatable Local Group illustration shows membership; its positions, sizes and directions are not measurable. Face-on and edge-on views use the same geometry, without computing galaxy evolution or stellar orbits.

narration.label: Put two bodies side by side
narration.text: Earth looks small beside Jupiter. Bring in the Sun and Jupiter becomes small; bring in Arcturus and even the Sun looks small. We compare diameters on one shared ruler. Placing them together does not mean they are physically close. Now meet enormous stars with catalogue-like names. With the estimates shown here, one placed at the Sun could reach around Saturn’s orbit. First imagine that size; then explore how astronomers estimate it.
narration.cue: Choose the three pairs or drag the slider, tracking the same retained body.

narration.label: A bigger ball or a bigger family?
narration.text: The Sun and its orbiting planets belong to the Solar System. Our Sun is one of many stars in the Milky Way. The Milky Way, Andromeda and many smaller galaxies belong to the Local Group. The Local Group and Virgo Cluster are different neighbors, yet both appear in the reconstructed Laniakea flow region. The cosmic web describes how such structures are distributed; it is not an outer shell.
narration.cue: Open the membership chapter and follow the five-stop address to the observable region; explore Virgo and a local web close-up separately.

narration.label: Turn the Milky Way around
narration.text: Find the Sun locator in the Milky Way. Face-on, starlight traces arms; turn edge-on and the same stars reveal a thin disk, a central bulge and a sparse stellar halo. The Sun stays in the disk. Compare a smooth elliptical galaxy and an asymmetric irregular galaxy. These are different examples, not stages of one galaxy changing shape. A star cluster is a collection of stars within a galaxy, not simply a miniature galaxy.
narration.cue: Open galaxy structure, choose face-on and edge-on, then drag to rotate. Toggle the disk, bulge and stellar halo; compare the cluster membership context with its independent close-up.

narration.label: Beyond our galaxy
narration.text: Keep the Sun’s place in the Milky Way in mind, then zoom continuously from Earth or the Sun. Fitting distant orbits into the view makes even the Sun’s disk invisible; its locator does not secretly enlarge it. The Milky Way shares the Local Group with many small galaxies, while Virgo is a separate neighbour. Farther out, the cosmic web illustrates a distribution. The final dashed horizon marks what can be observed from our location, not a wall around the universe. Today’s distance is not the light’s travel time.
narration.cue: Open continuous zoom, travel from the selected body through the Milky Way, Local Group and Laniakea distance scales to the observable region, and compare the linear ruler with the location labels.
